issues.legal_issue: The maximum penalty for an under-stamped instrument is discretionary and cannot be imposed mechanically or justified solely by an intention to evade stamp duty.
material_facts: The trustees executed a deed transferring property to beneficiaries, describing it as a deed of assent, although an earlier resolution contemplated a deed of transfer.
The deed was treated as a gift deed and had been stamped for only a small amount compared with the duty assessed as payable.
The Collector imposed the maximum penalty, reasoning that the document’s nature had not been disclosed with an intention to evade duty; the High Court relied on substantially the same reason.
Neither the Collector nor the High Court identified dishonest or contumacious conduct or gave any further reason supporting the maximum penalty.
issues.conclusion: The maximum penalty was not justified on the reasons given. The Court reduced it from ten times to five times the deficient duty and partly allowed the appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Section 40(1)(b) of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 makes a penalty up to ten times the proper duty or deficient portion discretionary through the words “if he thinks fit”; the maximum is not automatic and discretion must be exercised rationally and fairly. Read with Sections 33, 35, 38 and 39, the statutory scheme does not contemplate that the maximum penalty must ultimately be realised in every case. The Collector should consider relevant circumstances, including conduct and intent; mere evasion does not by itself justify the maximum, while fraud, deceit or undue enrichment may be relevant to its extent. A penalty is generally deterrent, not retributive. The Court relied on Gangtappa v. Fakkirappa, 2019 (3) SCC 788, on the statutory discretion to reduce or refund penalty, and Peteti Subba Rao v. Anumala S. Narendra, 2002 (10) SCC 427, which stated that the maximum is for very extreme situations and is not to be imposed as a matter of course.

rule.if: stamp_penalty_appeal and under_stamped_instrument and maximum_penalty_imposed and evasion_intent_was_only_reason and no_dishonest_or_contumacious_conduct_found

predicates.stamp_penalty_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the maximum penalty imposed for an under-stamped instrument.
predicates.under_stamped_instrument: The authority found that the instrument was chargeable with duty and had not been sufficiently stamped.
predicates.maximum_penalty_imposed: The authority imposed the highest penalty available for the deficient duty.
predicates.evasion_intent_was_only_reason: The authority relied only on an intention to evade duty as its reason for imposing the maximum penalty.
predicates.no_dishonest_or_contumacious_conduct_fou: The authority did not find that the person responsible for the instrument acted dishonestly or contumaciously.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns the maximum penalty for an under-stamped instrument and that maximum rests only on an intention to evade duty, without a finding of dishonest or contumacious conduct, the penalty is reduced below the maximum.
